title: Psalms Chapter 145 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 145 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 145 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 145.

questions.question: Who is the psalmist extolling in Psalms 145:1?
questions.correctAnswer: My God, O king
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:1 states, "I will extol thee, my God, O king" indicating the psalmist is praising God as king.

questions.question: How often does the psalmist say he will bless and praise God's name according to Psalms 145:2?
questions.correctAnswer: Every day
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:2 says, "Every day will I bless thee; and I will praise thy name for ever and ever."

questions.question: According to Psalms 145:3, how is the LORD described?
options: Great and greatly to be praised
questions.correctAnswer: Great and greatly to be praised
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:3 describes the LORD as "Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised; and his greatness is unsearchable."

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 145:4 says one generation will praise God's works to another.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:4 states clearly, "One generation shall praise thy works to another."

questions.question: What will the psalmist speak of according to Psalms 145:5?
options: The glorious honour of God's majesty and wondrous works
questions.correctAnswer: The glorious honour of God's majesty and wondrous works
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:5 says, "I will speak of the glorious honour of thy majesty, and of thy wondrous works."

questions.question: According to Psalms 145:6, who will speak of the mighty acts of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Men
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:6 says, "And men shall speak of the might of thy terrible acts."

questions.question: What will people abundantly utter and sing about according to Psalms 145:7?
options: The memory of God's great goodness and righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: The memory of God's great goodness and righteousness
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:7 says, "They shall abundantly utter the memory of thy great goodness, and shall sing of thy righteousness."

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 145:8 describes the LORD as slow to anger and full of compassion.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:8 states, "The LORD is gracious, and full of compassion; slow to anger, and of great mercy."

questions.question: According to Psalms 145:9, who is the LORD good to?
questions.correctAnswer: All
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:9 says, "The LORD is good to all: and his tender mercies are over all his works."

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 145:10 says that only the priests shall bless the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:10 states, "All thy works shall praise thee, O LORD; and thy saints shall bless thee." It does not limit blessing to priests.

questions.question: What will people speak of according to Psalms 145:11?
options: The glory of God's kingdom and His power
questions.correctAnswer: The glory of God's kingdom and His power
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:11 says, "They shall speak of the glory of thy kingdom, and talk of thy power;"

questions.question: According to Psalms 145:13, how is God's kingdom described?
options: Everlasting and enduring through all generations
questions.correctAnswer: Everlasting and enduring through all generations
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:13 states, "Thy kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and thy dominion endureth throughout all generations."

questions.question: Which comes first in Psalms 145:1-7: speaking of God's majesty or declaring His greatness?
options: Speaking of His majesty comes first
questions.correctAnswer: Speaking of His majesty comes first
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:5 says "I will speak of the glorious honour of thy majesty," and Psalms 145:6 follows with "I will declare thy greatness."

questions.question: According to Psalms 145:14, whom does the LORD uphold?
options: All that fall and those bowed down
questions.correctAnswer: All that fall and those bowed down
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:14 says, "The LORD upholdeth all that fall, and raiseth up all those that be bowed down."

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 145:15 teaches that the eyes of all wait upon the LORD for their food in due season.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:15 says, "The eyes of all wait upon thee; and thou givest them their meat in due season."

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 145 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 145 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 145:8, how is the LORD described in relation to human shortcomings?
options: Gracious, full of compassion, slow to anger, and of great mercy
Strict, unyielding, and quick to punish
questions.correctAnswer: Gracious, full of compassion, slow to anger, and of great mercy
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:8 explicitly states that the LORD is gracious and full of compassion, slow to anger, and of great mercy, highlighting His patience and kindness toward human failings.

questions.question: What does Psalms 145:9 teach about God's goodness and mercy?
options: The LORD is good to all, and His tender mercies are over all His works
God shows favor only to the righteous
His mercy is limited to Israel alone
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD is good to all, and His tender mercies are over all His works
questions.explanation: According to Psalms 145:9, God's goodness extends to everyone, and His tender mercies cover all His creations, emphasizing the universal nature of His care and kindness.

questions.question: What response does Psalms 145:10 indicate all of God's works and saints will have toward Him?
questions.correctAnswer: Praise and blessing
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:10 says all God's works shall praise Him, and His saints shall bless Him, showing that both creation and the faithful respond with worship and praise.

questions.question: How does Psalms 145:11 describe the message that God's people are to proclaim?
options: The glory of God's kingdom and His power
questions.correctAnswer: The glory of God's kingdom and His power
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that God's people shall speak of the glory of His kingdom and talk of His power, emphasizing the proclamation of God's majesty and strength.

questions.question: What is the purpose of making known God's mighty acts and the glorious majesty of His kingdom, according to Psalms 145:12?
options: To inform the sons of men
questions.correctAnswer: To inform the sons of men
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:12 states that the purpose is to make known to the sons of men God's mighty acts and the glorious majesty of His kingdom, meaning the message is intended for all humanity to learn about God's power and reign.

questions.question: According to Psalms 145:13, what is the nature and duration of God's kingdom and dominion?
options: Everlasting and enduring through all generations
questions.correctAnswer: Everlasting and enduring through all generations
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that God's kingdom is everlasting and His dominion endures throughout all generations, highlighting the eternal and unchanging nature of His rule.

questions.question: How does Psalms 145:14 describe God's care for those who are weak or discouraged?
options: He upholds all that fall and raises up those bowed down
He requires them to help themselves
questions.correctAnswer: He upholds all that fall and raises up those bowed down
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:14 teaches that the LORD supports and lifts up those who have fallen or are bowed down, emphasizing God's tender care for the weak and discouraged.

questions.question: What does Psalms 145:15 indicate about God's provision for His creation?
options: The eyes of all wait upon Him, and He gives them their meat in due season
He provides only for the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: The eyes of all wait upon Him, and He gives them their meat in due season
questions.explanation: This verse highlights God's faithful provision by stating that all creatures look to Him and He supplies their needs at the right time.

questions.question: According to Psalms 145:16, how does God satisfy the desires of living things?
options: By opening His hand and providing for every living thing
By limiting blessings to a select few
By testing their patience with scarcity
questions.correctAnswer: By opening His hand and providing for every living thing
questions.explanation: The verse describes God's generosity and care, indicating that He satisfies the desires of every living thing by generously providing for them.

questions.question: What does Psalms 145:17 teach about the moral character of the LORD's actions?
options: The LORD is righteous in all His ways and holy in all His works
The LORD acts unpredictably and without justice
The LORD is indifferent to human morality
The LORD only acts righteously towards some
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD is righteous in all His ways and holy in all His works
questions.explanation: This verse emphasizes God's perfect righteousness and holiness in every action He performs, reflecting His moral perfection.

questions.question: How does Psalms 145:18 describe God's nearness to those who seek Him?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:18 explicitly states that the LORD is near to all who call upon Him in truth, affirming God's closeness to sincere seekers.

questions.question: According to Psalms 145:19, what will God do for those who fear Him and call upon Him?
options: Fulfill their desires, hear their cry, and save them
Delay responding until they prove their faith
questions.correctAnswer: Fulfill their desires, hear their cry, and save them
questions.explanation: The verse promises that God will respond to those who fear Him by fulfilling their desires, hearing their cries, and saving them, showing His faithfulness and compassion.

questions.question: What contrasting outcomes are described in Psalms 145:20 for those who love the LORD versus the wicked?
options: God preserves those who love Him but destroys the wicked
God ignores both the righteous and the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: God preserves those who love Him but destroys the wicked
questions.explanation: The verse contrasts God's preservation of those who love Him with His destruction of the wicked, emphasizing the consequences of one's relationship with God.

questions.question: What is the significance of the promise in Psalms 145:19 when combined with the description of God in Psalms 145:8 and Psalms 145:18?
options: God, being gracious and near to those who call upon Him in truth, will fulfill their desires and save them
God is distant and slow to respond to prayers
God punishes those who fear Him without mercy
God only helps those who perform miracles
questions.correctAnswer: God, being gracious and near to those who call upon Him in truth, will fulfill their desires and save them
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:8 describes God as gracious and compassionate; Psalms 145:18 says He is near to those who call upon Him in truth; and Psalms 145:19 promises He will fulfill their desires and save them, showing a consistent message of God's loving responsiveness.

questions.question: How does the message in Psalms 145:10 and Psalms 145:11 guide believers in their daily walk of faith?
options: Believers and creation are called to praise God and proclaim His kingdom and power
Believers should keep their faith private and not speak of God's kingdom
Only priests are responsible for praising God
Believers should focus on earthly kingdoms instead
questions.correctAnswer: Believers and creation are called to praise God and proclaim His kingdom and power
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:10 states all God’s works praise Him and saints bless Him, while Psalms 145:11 calls for speaking of His kingdom and power, guiding believers to active praise and proclamation.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 145 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 145.

questions.question: According to Psalms 145:15, what do the eyes of all wait upon?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:15 states that 'The eyes of all wait upon thee,' referring to the LORD as the one whom all look to for provision.

questions.question: What does Psalms 145:16 say the LORD does to satisfy the desires of every living thing?
questions.correctAnswer: He opens His hand
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:16 says, 'Thou openest thine hand, and satisfiest the desire of every living thing,' indicating God's generous provision.

questions.question: What two qualities are attributed to the LORD in Psalms 145:17?
questions.correctAnswer: Righteousness and holiness
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:17 states, 'The LORD is righteous in all his ways, and holy in all his works,' emphasizing God's just and pure nature.

questions.question: According to Psalms 145:18, to whom is the LORD particularly near?
options: All that call upon him in truth
questions.correctAnswer: All that call upon him in truth
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:18 says, 'The LORD is nigh unto all them that call upon him, to all that call upon him in truth,' highlighting God's closeness to sincere worshipers.

questions.question: What will the LORD do for those that fear Him, according to Psalms 145:19?
options: Fulfil their desires, hear their cry, and save them
questions.correctAnswer: Fulfil their desires, hear their cry, and save them
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:19 promises that God 'will fulfil the desire of them that fear him: he also will hear their cry, and will save them,' assuring His faithful care.

questions.question: What is the fate of the wicked according to Psalms 145:20?
questions.correctAnswer: They will be destroyed
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:20 states, 'but all the wicked will he destroy,' indicating God's judgment upon the wicked.

questions.question: How does Psalms 145:21 express the psalmist's commitment to praising the LORD?
options: My mouth shall speak the praise of the LORD
I will sing only in the temple
I will write songs for kings
I will remain silent in trials
questions.correctAnswer: My mouth shall speak the praise of the LORD
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'My mouth shall speak the praise of the LORD,' showing the psalmist's dedication to continual praise.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of God providing for all creatures as in Psalms 145:15-16?
options: Matthew 6:26 - Consider the lilies of the field
Genesis 1:1 - Creation of the heavens and earth
Revelation 21:4 - New heaven and new earth
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 6:26 - Consider the lilies of the field
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:26 parallels Psalms 145:15-16 by illustrating God's provision for all living things, including birds and lilies.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word translated as 'mercies' in Psalms 145:9, and how does it relate to God's character?
options: Compassionate lovingkindness; it shows God’s enduring kindness over all His works
Strength; it shows God’s power over His creation
questions.correctAnswer: Compassionate lovingkindness; it shows God’s enduring kindness over all His works
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'mercies' (חסד, chesed) implies steadfast lovingkindness, reflecting God's faithful compassion as stated in Psalms 145:9.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Psalms 145 to emphasize God's enduring praise from generation to generation?
options: Inclusio framing the psalm with eternal praise
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio framing the psalm with eternal praise
questions.explanation: Psalms 145 begins and ends with praise 'for ever and ever' (verses 1 and 21), forming an inclusio emphasizing eternal worship.

questions.question: Which passage in the New Testament reflects the promise in Psalms 145:18 about God being near to those who call on Him in truth?
options: James 4:8 - Draw nigh to God, and He will draw nigh to you
John 3:16 - God so loved the world
Romans 8:28 - All things work together for good
Hebrews 11:1 - Faith is the substance of things hoped for
questions.correctAnswer: James 4:8 - Draw nigh to God, and He will draw nigh to you
questions.explanation: James 4:8 echoes Psalms 145:18 by emphasizing God's nearness to those who sincerely seek Him.

questions.question: How does the promise in Psalms 145:19 about fulfilling the desires of those who fear Him connect to Old Testament covenant themes?
options: It reflects God's faithfulness to His covenant people as in Deuteronomy 7:9
It contradicts the covenant blessings in Exodus
It is unrelated to covenant themes
It focuses only on new covenant promises
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects God's faithfulness to His covenant people as in Deuteronomy 7:9
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 7:9 underscores God's covenant faithfulness, paralleling Psalms 145:19's promise to those who fear Him.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 145:20 states that the LORD preserves all who love Him but ignores the wicked.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:20 says, 'The LORD preserveth all them that love him: but all the wicked will he destroy,' indicating the LORD actively destroys the wicked rather than ignoring them.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 145:21 calls for all flesh to bless the LORD’s holy name forever and ever.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:21 clearly states, 'let all flesh bless his holy name for ever and ever,' calling universal praise to God.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage also highlights God's care for the weak as Psalms 145:14 does by saying He upholds all that fall?
options: Psalm 37:24 - He shall not be moved
Isaiah 53:5 - He was bruised for our iniquities
Exodus 14:21 - Parting of the Red Sea
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 37:24 - He shall not be moved
questions.explanation: Psalm 37:24, like Psalms 145:14, emphasizes God's support for those who stumble, showing His care for the weak.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 145 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 145 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is primarily highlighted in Psalms 145:8?
questions.correctAnswer: God's grace and compassion
questions.explanation: Psalms 145:8 emphasizes that 'The LORD is gracious, and full of compassion; slow to anger, and of great mercy,' directly revealing God's grace and compassion.

questions.question: What does Psalms 145:13 teach about the nature of God's kingdom?
options: It is everlasting and enduring through all generations
It is only for the righteous
It is established through human effort
questions.correctAnswer: It is everlasting and enduring through all generations
questions.explanation: Verse 13 clearly states, 'Thy kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and thy dominion endureth throughout all generations,' emphasizing the eternal and unending nature of God's kingdom.

questions.question: According to Psalms 145:14, what does the LORD do for those who fall and are bowed down?
options: He waits for them to recover on their own
questions.correctAnswer: He upholds and raises them
questions.explanation: Verse 14 states, 'The LORD upholdeth all that fall, and raiseth up all those that be bowed down,' showing God's sustaining and restorative power for the weak.

questions.question: What combined teaching about God's providence and care is conveyed by Psalms 145:15 and Psalms 145:16?
options: God is indifferent to creation's needs
God provides for all beings in due time and satisfies their desires
God only provides for the righteous
God's provision is limited and conditional
questions.correctAnswer: God provides for all beings in due time and satisfies their desires
questions.explanation: Verse 15 says, 'The eyes of all wait upon thee; and thou givest them their meat in due season,' and verse 16, 'Thou openest thine hand, and satisfiest the desire of every living thing,' together affirm God's universal providence and timely provision.

questions.question: How does Psalms 145:18 describe God's accessibility to those who seek Him?
options: God is near to all who call upon Him in truth
God only listens to the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: God is near to all who call upon Him in truth
questions.explanation: Verse 18 states, 'The LORD is nigh unto all them that call upon him, to all that call upon him in truth,' emphasizing God's nearness and accessibility to sincere seekers.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine justice and salvation is taught in Psalms 145:19-20?
options: God saves all people without distinction
God fulfills the desires of those who fear Him and preserves those who love Him, but destroys the wicked
God ignores the cries of the fearful
God's justice is arbitrary and unpredictable
questions.correctAnswer: God fulfills the desires of those who fear Him and preserves those who love Him, but destroys the wicked
questions.explanation: Verses 19-20 teach that 'He will fulfil the desire of them that fear him... The LORD preserveth all them that love him: but all the wicked will he destroy,' highlighting God's justice in salvation and judgment.

questions.question: What theological truth about human praise and worship is emphasized in Psalms 145:10 and Psalms 145:21?
options: Only angels can truly praise God
All creation and all flesh should bless and praise God's holy name forever
Only the Old Testament saints are called to bless God
questions.correctAnswer: All creation and all flesh should bless and praise God's holy name forever
questions.explanation: Verse 10 says, 'All thy works shall praise thee, O LORD; and thy saints shall bless thee,' and verse 21 concludes, 'My mouth shall speak the praise of the LORD: and let all flesh bless his holy name for ever and ever,' stressing universal, eternal praise.

questions.question: What does Psalms 145:3 reveal about the nature of God's greatness?
options: God's greatness is fully known to humanity
God's greatness is unsearchable and beyond full human comprehension
God's greatness depends on human understanding
God's greatness is limited by creation
questions.correctAnswer: God's greatness is unsearchable and beyond full human comprehension
questions.explanation: Verse 3 states, 'Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised; and his greatness is unsearchable,' affirming the infinite and incomprehensible nature of God's greatness.

questions.question: According to Psalms 145:4, what is the role of successive generations in relation to God's works?
options: Each generation should forget previous acts
One generation shall praise God's works to another and declare His mighty acts
Generations should compete to outdo each other's praise
Only the first generation is responsible for praising God
questions.correctAnswer: One generation shall praise God's works to another and declare His mighty acts
questions.explanation: Verse 4 teaches that God's works and mighty acts are to be passed down and proclaimed from one generation to the next, ensuring continuous praise.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God's mercy is limited and conditional. What does Psalms 145:9 actually teach about God's mercy?
options: God's mercy is only for a select few
God's tender mercies are over all His works, showing universal mercy
God's mercy is irrelevant to His works
questions.correctAnswer: God's tender mercies are over all His works, showing universal mercy
questions.explanation: Verse 9 states, 'The LORD is good to all: and his tender mercies are over all his works,' demonstrating that God's mercy extends universally, countering sceptical claims.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about God's kingdom and power is taught in Psalms 145:11-12?
options: God's kingdom is temporary and His power is limited
They speak of the glory and power of God's kingdom and make known His mighty acts and majesty to mankind
God's kingdom is hidden and unknowable
God's power is only for angels
questions.correctAnswer: They speak of the glory and power of God's kingdom and make known His mighty acts and majesty to mankind
questions.explanation: Verses 11-12 reveal that God's kingdom is glorious and powerful, and His mighty acts and majesty are to be proclaimed to all people, emphasizing His sovereign rule.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted in Psalms 145:17 regarding His moral character?
options: God is forgiving in some ways but unjust in others
God is righteous and holy in all His ways and works
God is indifferent to human morality
questions.correctAnswer: God is righteous and holy in all His ways and works
questions.explanation: Verse 17 states, 'The LORD is righteous in all his ways, and holy in all his works,' underscoring the perfect righteousness and holiness of God.

questions.question: How does Psalms 145:5-6 contribute to the understanding of the purpose of declaring God's works?
options: To speak of the glorious honor and might of God's majesty and terrible acts, declaring His greatness
questions.correctAnswer: To speak of the glorious honor and might of God's majesty and terrible acts, declaring His greatness
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 express the intent to proclaim God's majestic honor and mighty acts, highlighting the purpose of praise and declaration of His greatness.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight about God's preservation and judgment arises from synthesizing Psalms 145:19 and Psalms 145:20?
options: God is indifferent to human love and fear
God listens to those who fear Him and preserves those who love Him, but will destroy all the wicked
God preserves everyone regardless of their heart
questions.correctAnswer: God listens to those who fear Him and preserves those who love Him, but will destroy all the wicked
questions.explanation: These verses together affirm that God is attentive and responsive to the faithful, preserving them, while executing judgment on the wicked, revealing His just character.

questions.question: What does Psalms 145:7 teach about the response of people to God's goodness and righteousness?
options: People shall abundantly utter the memory of God's great goodness and sing of His righteousness
People will remain silent about God's works
questions.correctAnswer: People shall abundantly utter the memory of God's great goodness and sing of His righteousness
questions.explanation: Verse 7 reveals that people are called to extensively proclaim God's goodness and righteousness through praise and remembrance.
